phase_name: Permission Broker Foundation Policy Applicability Contract Freeze
summary: Normative contract-freeze phase (no src/pcae/** file modified, confirmed via git diff --name-only 0923b76d..HEAD -- src/pcae/, empty; no runtime-capability change, confirmed via pcae runtime inspect before/after: Observed / observe / unavailable, unchanged). Independently re-verified every load-bearing claim in Phase 148C.2's design against primary source (the Foundation's own module docstring/design principles and evaluate_all mechanism, NG-008's exact scope statement, the Phase 109 command-category table's 'POL-004 approval where applicable' text, the PR-compatible workflow Section 5 Git Approval / Execution Approval separation, MissingHumanApprovalRule's unconditional condition, execution_class's required-field status, POLICY_IDS/DEFAULT_POLICY_RULES fixed-tuple status, the empty-registry-DENY and malformed-result-DENY fail-closed mechanics) and found zero discrepancies. Froze PBPA-001 v1.0 -- Permission Broker Policy Applicability Contract (docs/contracts/PERMISSION_BROKER_POLICY_APPLICABILITY_CONTRACT.md, 114 PBPA-REQ-### requirements), selecting the PBPA-001 identifier by surveying every existing docs/contracts/*.md identifier and applying this repository's own established initialism convention. Freezes: the applicability/evaluation separation (applicability resolved from execution_class alone, strictly before approval_present/evidence_available are read); a per-policy APPLICABLE/NOT_APPLICABLE result model with no fourth broker-level decision value (ALLOW/DENY/HUMAN_REVIEW remain the only three); the selected hybrid architecture (declarative, policy-owned, registry-enforced applicable_execution_classes, never caller-selectable, no exclude_policies parameter authorized anywhere); a complete, independently re-derived POL-001..012 applicability matrix (POL-001/003/005/006/007 universal; POL-004 scoped to {shell, backend, adapter, rollback} via a general rule stated once, explicitly not a push-specific carve-out; POL-002/008/009 moot-universal stubs; POL-010/011/012 stubs with eventual scope deliberately left UNRESOLVED and deferred to their future implementing phase); a full classification-authenticity/anti-spoofing threat model (execution_class contract-fixed per integration point, never caller-discretionary per request); fail-closed defaults for every unknown/missing/malformed/duplicate condition (always toward evaluating more policies, never fewer); determinism, versioning (travels with the Foundation contract, no separate artifact), explainability (additive applicable_policy_ids/non_applicable_policy_ids fields, no durable audit artifact authorized), and a full contract-compatibility review (PBPC-001 v1.1 not amended). Does not close B-1 -- contract text only, unimplemented, unverified; the remaining closure path is documented (independent verification -> Foundation implementation -> implementation verification -> PBPC-001 v1.2 re-evaluation -> B-1 re-verification). No Blocking architectural conflict with any frozen contract was found. See docs/PHASE_148C.3_PERMISSION_BROKER_FOUNDATION_POLICY_APPLICABILITY_CONTRACT_FREEZE.md and docs/contracts/PERMISSION_BROKER_POLICY_APPLICABILITY_CONTRACT.md for full detail. Verdict: POLICY APPLICABILITY CONTRACT FROZEN -- READY FOR INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. B-1 NOT CLOSED.
